page.title: Event Run of Show Timeline Guide
page.description: Learn what a run of show timeline includes, when to start, who owns each workstream, and how to rehearse and escalate late assets.
page.h1: How long does an event run of show take to build and lock?
page.definition: A run of show timeline is a minute-by-minute production plan that assigns every cue, speaker, graphic, and backup stream to a named owner from rehearsal through live delivery and post-event replay.
page.quick_answer: Start the run of show two to three weeks before a webinar or six to eight weeks before a summit; lock speaker slides and lower thirds at least five days out and run one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before going live.

sections.h2: What workstreams belong in a run of show timeline?

blocks.p: A complete run of show breaks into eight workstreams, each with a single owner and a concrete output that feeds the next stage.

head: Workstream
Owner
Output
rows: Confirmed bios, slides, and tech specs

sections.h2: When should you start building the run of show?

blocks.p: Lead time depends on event size: a webinar needs three to four weeks from brief to live, while a summit or online conference requires six to eight weeks of management.

ul: Week one: intake brief, confirm platform, assign workstream owners
Week two: collect speaker slides, bios, and technical requirements
Week three: build branded templates, lower thirds, and scene layouts
Week four: load assets into platform, configure polls and Q&A
Week five (summit): integrate venue AV, test hybrid signal paths
Week six (summit): full speaker rehearsals on the real platform
Final week: technical check 60 minutes before go-live, backup stream verified

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and rehearsal schedule?

blocks.p: Staffing scales with complexity: one producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, and platform operator each owning a workstream.

ol: Show caller owns the master script and calls every cue live
Speaker manager confirms slides, bios, and tech checks for every presenter
Platform operator builds scenes, loads media, and monitors stream health
Moderator runs the question queue and escalates issues to the show caller
Producer coordinates rehearsals, distributes feedback, and locks final assets

sections.h2: What does a rehearsal schedule look like?

blocks.p: Plan one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event, plus a technical check 60 minutes before going live.

ul: Day minus five: speaker tech checks (audio, camera, screen share)
Day minus three: full run-through with all cues, graphics, and playback
Day minus two: incorporate feedback, lock final slide order and lower thirds
Day minus one: dry run with moderator and Q&A flow
Go-live minus 60 minutes: final signal test, backup stream handshake, cue sheet review

sections.h2: How do you handle late assets and escalation?

blocks.p: Late slides, missing bios, or untested videos are the top risk; build a hard cutoff and a clear escalation ladder into the run of show.

ul: Asset freeze: speaker slides and videos due five days before rehearsal
Escalation tier one: speaker manager contacts presenter within four hours of miss
Escalation tier two: producer alerts show caller and adjusts script buffers
Escalation tier three: executive sponsor notified if gap threatens live flow
Backup plan: placeholder graphic and scripted host transition for any missing segment

faq.q: Can I reuse a run of show template for recurring webinars?
faq.a: Yes. A repeat format can move faster because the agenda structure, graphic templates, and platform scenes stay consistent; only speaker-specific assets and timing buffers need updating each cycle.

faq.q: What platform features must be configured in the run of show?
faq.a: Scene layouts, poll timing, Q&A moderation settings, recording start and stop cues, backup stream ingest points, and closed-caption toggles all belong in the run of show so the platform operator executes them on cue.

faq.q: How do I staff a hybrid event run of show differently from a virtual one?
faq.a: Hybrid adds a venue AV lead, a signal engineer for the in-room to cloud bridge, and a dedicated camera operator; the show caller then cues both the virtual platform and the physical stage from one master script.

faq.q: When should the edited replay and clips be delivered?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event; highlight clips for social follow the same deadline to keep momentum in the owned audience channels.
